To start we import the packages, which are built-in to R.


::: {#2 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.julia .cell-code}
using Pkg
Pkg.activate(".")
Pkg.add("StatsKit")
Pkg.add("DataFrames")
```
:::





Next, we can fit the simple intercept-only model.


::: {#4 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.julia .cell-code}
using Distributions, DataFrames, GLM, StatsModels, CategoricalArrays

df = DataFrame(mass=[60,80,50,70,90,110], 
                pop=categorical([1,1,2,2,3,3]), 
                reg=categorical([1,1,1,1,2,2]), 
                hab=categorical([1,2,3,1,2,3]))

intercept_model = lm(@formula(mass ~ 1), df)
intercept_model
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1}
```
StatsModels.TableRegressionModel{LinearModel{GLM.LmResp{Vector{Float64}}, GLM.DensePredChol{Float64, LinearAlgebra.CholeskyPivoted{Float64, Matrix{Float64}, Vector{Int64}}}}, Matrix{Float64}}

mass ~ 1

Coefficients:
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
               Coef.  Std. Error     t  Pr(>|t|)  Lower 95%  Upper 95%
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
(Intercept)  76.6667     8.81917  8.69    0.0003    53.9963    99.3371
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```
:::
:::





For t-test equivalent


::: {#6 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.julia .cell-code}
model_ttest = lm(@formula(mass ~ reg), df)
display(model_ttest)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
```
StatsModels.TableRegressionModel{LinearModel{GLM.LmResp{Vector{Float64}}, GLM.DensePredChol{Float64, LinearAlgebra.CholeskyPivoted{Float64, Matrix{Float64}, Vector{Int64}}}}, Matrix{Float64}}

mass ~ 1 + reg

Coefficients:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Coef.  Std. Error     t  Pr(>|t|)  Lower 95%  Upper 95%
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
(Intercept)   65.0     6.61438  9.83    0.0006   46.6355     83.3645
reg: 2        35.0    11.4564   3.06    0.0378    3.19183    66.8082
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```
:::
:::





The docs say we can use modelmatrix as a convenience to extract the design matrix from a formula and a DataFrame. Unlike R, a formula that omits the left-hand side is not permitted.


::: {#8 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.julia .cell-code}
model_matrix = modelmatrix(@formula(mass ~ reg), df)
display(model_matrix)
```
